answer: Cross-cluster attestation quorums bind identity to graph position. Each agent's voyage through an epoch must collect a pearl of attestation from peers outside its own cluster; the network cuts the trust graph along non-kin edges and rejects identities whose attestations concentrate in one region. An attacker running 500 clones finds every fake voyage routing through the same parent wallets, and one cross-cluster audit catches the ripple of self-vouching. Each pearl must come from a distinct graph region, so attacker cost scales linearly with identity count while honest cost stays near zero.
